topic: Open car differential: why the outer wheel can turn faster in a turn (spider gears on the carrier pin spin only when the wheel speeds differ).
title: How a Car Differential Works 🚗
principle: The pinion turns the ring gear, which is bolted to the carrier; the carrier holds spider gears on a cross-pin that mesh with the two side gears on the axle shafts. Straight ahead the spiders do not turn on their pin, so both wheels turn at carrier speed; in a turn they spin on the pin, letting one side gear run faster and the other slower by the same amount (carrier speed = average of the wheel speeds; one wheel held = the other at twice carrier speed).
voiceover: How can two wheels on one axle turn at different speeds?
In a turn, the outer wheel travels a longer path than the inner wheel.
With a solid axle, one tire would have to skid.
So in the middle, there's a differential.
The driveshaft turns the ring gear. Its spider gears mesh with a side gear on each axle.
Going straight, the spider gears ride along, but they don't turn on their pin. So both wheels turn at the same speed.
In a turn, the road slows the inner wheel. Now the spider gears turn on their pin, and the outer wheel speeds up by the same amount.
Hold one wheel still: the other spins at twice the ring gear's speed.
The spider gears let one wheel slow down while the other speeds up.

firstComment:
Answer: twice as fast 🔧

In a turn, the outer wheel rolls along a bigger circle than the inner one, so it has to turn faster. With a solid axle, one tire would have to scrub.

The pinion on the driveshaft turns the big ring gear. The ring gear is bolted to the carrier, and the carrier holds small spider gears on a pin. The spider gears mesh with the two side gears, one on each axle shaft.

Going straight, the spider gears don't turn on their pin: everything spins as one block and both wheels turn at the same speed. In a turn, the spider gears start to spin on the pin, so one side gear runs slower and the other faster by the same amount. The ring gear always turns at the average of the two wheel speeds, so if one wheel is held still, the other spins at twice the ring gear's speed.

(Simplified 3D model: an open differential with two spider gears and straight bevel teeth; real axles use hypoid gears, and the car body is shown see-through.)

Sources:
Britannica, Differential gear (on a straight road no relative motion between side gears and pinions; in a left turn the right wheel turns faster; the ring gear turns at the mean speed of the two wheels): https://www.britannica.com/technology/differential-gear
MIT 2.972, How a Differential Works (straight: the planet pinions do not spin; w_in = (w1 + w2) / 2): https://web.mit.edu/2.972/www/reports/differential/differential.html
tec-science, How does a differential gear work? (one wheel standing still, the other turns at double speed): https://www.tec-science.com/mechanical-power-transmission/planetary-gear/how-does-a-differential-gear-work
Counterman, Limited-Slip Differentials (spider gears ride on a pin in the carrier; they don't spin going straight and spin on the pin in a corner): https://www.counterman.com/limited-slip-differentials
